site.name: booking
site.summary: booking-clone Clone of the Booking.com hotel booking funnel (home → city list → area filters → detail → room → booking → confirmation), plus other business-line and supporting pages. Pages | File | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `index.html` | Home: search bar (destination / check-in & out dates / guests), recommended destinations, recent searches, Genius membership prompt, business-line entries in the footer | | `tokyo.html` | Tokyo hotel list: left filter panel (price, stars, rating, amenities, area), right-hand hotel cards (price, rating, review count, distance, free-cancellation tag), sort bar, map entry | | `shinjuku.html` | Shinjuku-area hotel list, same structure as above, pre-filtered to Shinjuku |

explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full booking system, prioritizing the primary checkout/booking flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: The core hotel funnel is generally understandable: search leads to results, hotel detail and room-selection preserve key context, and confirmation gives strong success feedback with booking details and next steps. The biggest UX weaknesses are in result filtering/sorting trust and the mobile checkout layout, where overflow, tiny targets, and weak progress feedback make completion feel brittle. Coverage spans all pages, but only a small share of interactive elements were directly exercised, so some supporting flows remain only partially validated.

exploration_plan.goal: Explore and critique the Booking.com-style booking experience end to end, with deepest coverage on the hotel booking funnel from home/search through confirmation, while also sampling adjacent travel products, account/support pages, and post-booking management states on desktop and mobile.
exploration_plan.summary: Start by validating the primary hotel funnel that the prescan clearly exposes: index.html → tokyo/shinjuku results → hotel detail → room selection → reservation → confirmation. Then expand into nearby decision and recovery paths such as reviews, my trips, help, sign-in/register, and the secondary business lines surfaced in the global nav. Because several pages show dense filters, many small tap targets, and some missing input labels, prioritize interaction clarity, state persistence, and mobile usability on search/listing and booking form pages.
assumptions: The main hotel flow is statically linked and should be traversable via visible links/buttons rather than a true backend search submission.
Tokyo/Shinjuku pages represent the intended listing/filter experience for the primary accommodation funnel.
Confirmation, my-trips, and support pages are available as post-booking and recovery states rather than requiring authenticated backend data.
Secondary flows available for exploration are limited to the pages seen in prescan: flights, car rentals, attractions, airport taxis, deals, list-property, help, sign-in, and register.
risk_hotspots: index.html search bar inputs and Search CTA: core entry point, visible as inputs without a form, needs validation of affordance and routing
tokyo.html filter panel and sort controls: very high control density with 35 inputs and a visible 'No properties match your filters' state worth provoking/checking
shinjuku.html pre-filtered results and empty-state behavior: confirm area-specific filtering, card quality, and reset/discoverability
hotel-detail.html availability/reserve area: critical bridge from browsing to booking, needs pricing/date consistency and CTA clarity
hotel-detail-granbell.html reserve path: secondary property comparison path to ensure alternate hotel pages behave consistently
reviews.html sort dropdown and traveler-type tabs: check content filtering, state changes, and readability of social proof
room-selection.html price summary and onward CTA: verify selected room, taxes, cancellation, and 'Continue to booking details' continuity
reservation.html guest details form: 12 inputs, radio choices, special requests, arrival time/payment/cancellation messaging, and at least one missing input label
confirmation.html booking summary and next-step links: verify final-state completeness, reassurance, and cross-sell intrusiveness
my-trips.html tabs and action buttons like Cancel booking / Modify dates / Write a review / Book again: post-booking management and recovery affordances
flights.html trip-type radios, cabin-class select, and search/results relationship: multi-control search UI complexity
car-rentals.html 'Drop car off at different location' control and search/result cards: checkbox/toggle clarity plus deal CTA flow
airport-taxis.html unlabeled inputs and repeated Book CTAs: transport-booking clarity and transfer option comparison
help.html search plus topic cards and chat/call actions: support discoverability and escalation paths
signin.html and register.html account-entry forms: form clarity, password expectations, alternate sign-in buttons, and low-friction routing
Mobile nav/header controls across pages: prescan already shows many small tap targets in top navigation and footer/support links

phases.title: Primary hotel discovery and search entry
phases.objective: Validate how a user starts a stay search from the homepage and reaches browseable hotel results, including alternative discovery links.
key_checks: Use the home search inputs as presented and activate Search to confirm expected routing into results
Compare entry via homepage Search versus Tokyo destination cards/links to see whether the same results context is reached
Inspect search-field defaults and whether destination/date/guest context is visible and understandable on results pages
Exercise at least several Tokyo/Shinjuku filters and a sort option to check discoverability, feedback, and whether results/empty-state messaging stays coherent
If possible, trigger or inspect the visible 'No properties match your filters' state and assess recoverability/reset options
Check map entry visibility and usefulness as surfaced in the list pages
exit_criteria: A repeatable path from index.html to hotel results is confirmed
At least one listing page filter interaction and one sort interaction have been exercised
Evidence is gathered on whether search context and result counts remain understandable after changes

phases.title: Property evaluation and selection
phases.objective: Assess how effectively listing pages support comparison and how hotel detail/reviews pages help users decide before booking.
key_checks: Open at least two property details from results, including Park Hyatt Tokyo and Shinjuku Granbell Hotel, to compare consistency of layout and CTA prominence
Validate breadcrumb/back-to-results behavior and whether users can easily return to browsing without losing context
Check that core decision info is easy to find: location score, review count, facilities, highlights, pricing for 3 nights, and availability area
Enter or inspect guest reviews from the property flow and exercise review sorting and traveler-type filters
Look for mismatches between listing-card promises and property-detail specifics such as free cancellation, breakfast, and pricing framing
exit_criteria: Two hotel detail pages have been inspected and compared
At least one route into reviews.html has been exercised
Booking-decision information hierarchy and any inconsistencies between list/detail/reviews have been documented

phases.title: Checkout and confirmation funnel
phases.objective: Walk the main reservation funnel end to end and validate continuity, clarity, and trust signals from room choice through confirmation.
key_checks: Use the property reserve/availability path to enter room-selection.html and confirm room/date/guest details carry forward
Validate price summary structure across room selection, reservation, and confirmation, including taxes, city tax, cancellation timing, and payment timing
Complete reservation form interactions using visible fields: first name, last name, email, country/region, phone, booking-for-self/other, and special requests
Check required-field signaling, label clarity, placeholder dependence, and whether form sections like arrival time/payment schedule/cancellation are understandable
Proceed to confirmation and verify booking reference, property details, dates, room details, and reassurance content are complete and internally consistent
Assess whether cross-sell links on confirmation support the user without overwhelming the completed-booking state
exit_criteria: A full path from hotel detail to confirmation is completed
Continuity of selected room, price, and policy information across all checkout pages is verified
At least one form-quality issue or success pattern is captured from reservation.html

phases.title: Post-booking management, support, and account access
phases.objective: Test adjacent flows users rely on after or around booking: trip management, support, sign-in, and registration.
key_checks: From confirmation and/or global/footer nav, enter my-trips.html and test tabs such as Upcoming, Completed, and Cancelled
Exercise visible trip actions including View details, Cancel booking, Modify dates, Write a review, and Book again where available
Use help.html search and topic tiles to assess findability of cancellation, payment/refund, change-booking, and account/security help
Inspect chat and call CTAs for prominence and expected behavior
Review sign-in and registration flows for input clarity, password expectations, alternate auth options, and smooth cross-linking between sign in and create account
exit_criteria: Trip-management and support pages have each had multiple visible controls exercised
At least one recovery-oriented path is validated from booking/confirmation into support or management
Sign-in and register pages are both inspected for UX blockers and consistency

phases.title: Secondary product lines and mobile verification
phases.objective: Sample the non-hotel business lines linked in global navigation and repeat critical checks on mobile for responsiveness and tap usability.
key_checks: Visit each secondary product page from the nav or direct route and exercise its main search/filter CTA at least once
In flights.html, switch among trip types and inspect cabin-class select plus results-to-selection affordance
In car-rentals.html, toggle 'Drop car off at different location' and inspect deal-card progression
In attractions.html and airport-taxis.html, compare search clarity, card content, and booking CTA prominence
Inspect deals.html and list-property.html as promotional/partner-entry experiences for relevance and navigation quality

On mobile viewport, repeat the critical hotel flow checkpoints on index, results, hotel detail, reservation, and my-trips, focusing on header nav, tap-target size, filter usability, and form completion
exit_criteria: All secondary-nav pages discovered in prescan have been visited and at least lightly exercised
Critical mobile checks are completed on the main hotel path plus one post-booking page
Responsive issues and small-tap-target impacts are documented with concrete examples

coverage_targets.pages: Visit all 19 known HTML pages, with deepest interaction coverage on index.html, tokyo.html, shinjuku.html, hotel-detail.html, room-selection.html, reservation.html, confirmation.html, my-trips.html, and help.html.
coverage_targets.features: Exercise most visible controls on key pages: homepage search, listing filters/sort/map entry, property reserve/reviews links, room-selection onward CTA, reservation form fields/radios/textarea, confirmation next steps, my-trips tabs/actions, help search/topics, sign-in/register forms, and the primary search/booking controls on each secondary product page.
coverage_targets.mobile: Repeat critical checks on mobile viewport for the main hotel funnel (index → results → hotel detail → reservation → confirmation) plus my-trips and one secondary product page, with emphasis on navigation collapse/clarity, tap target adequacy, dense filter interaction, and form readability.

notes: Do not spend disproportionate time on placeholder links with href '#'; prefer pages and controls with real navigable destinations seen in the prescan.

Prescan shows repeated small tap-target warnings across nav/footer plus missing input labels on airport-taxis.html, attractions.html, car-rentals.html, reservation.html, tokyo.html, and shinjuku.html; treat these as likely recurring usability themes to verify rather than assume.
Because there are no prescan-reported console or network errors, prioritize UX flow quality, consistency, and responsiveness over technical fault hunting.

findings.user_goal: Complete a booking on mobile without layout-related friction
findings.problem: Multiple key mobile booking pages are wider than the viewport, causing horizontal overflow and partially off-screen content during the funnel.
findings.evidence: Observed overflow on hotel-detail-granbell.html (812px content on 390px viewport), room-selection.html (713px on 390px), reservation.html (814px on 390px), and confirmation.html (633px on 390px). Recent screenshots and observations note content/cards cut off to the right and header links extending off-screen.
findings.why_it_matters: Overflow makes users pan horizontally to read or act, increases the chance of missing important fields/CTAs, and makes a high-stakes checkout feel unreliable on mobile.
findings.suggestion: Fix responsive layouts for the booking funnel first: ensure containers, cards, headers, and form rows collapse to a single-column mobile layout with no horizontal scroll.

findings.user_goal: Understand whether filters are working and trust the hotel results shown
findings.problem: The results pages present contradictory state messaging, showing available properties while also surfacing a 'No properties match your filters' heading.
findings.evidence: Repeated observations on tokyo.html and shinjuku.html report visible hotel cards and counts like 'Tokyo: 6 properties found', 'Tokyo: 4 properties found', 'Tokyo: 3 properties found', and 'Shinjuku: 423 properties found' while the DOM simultaneously contains the heading 'No properties match your filters'.
findings.why_it_matters: Conflicting messages make users doubt whether the listings are current, whether filters applied correctly, and whether they should adjust or clear filters.
findings.suggestion: Ensure only one state is rendered/announced at a time: either show results with counts and active chips, or a true empty state with recovery actions such as removing filters.
findings.source_hint: tokyo.html and shinjuku.html results header / empty-state region

findings.user_goal: Use price filters to find hotels within budget
findings.problem: Budget filters do not match the visible prices users see, making the filtering logic hard to understand.
findings.evidence: After selecting bands such as 'JPY 10,000 - 20,000', 'JPY 20,000 - 40,000', and 'JPY 40,000 - 80,000', visible cards still showed much higher totals like JPY 198,000, JPY 245,000, and JPY 135,000. Observations explicitly flagged this mismatch several times on tokyo.html.
findings.why_it_matters: If users cannot tell whether the budget is nightly, total stay, or something else, they cannot confidently compare options or trust the filter system.
findings.suggestion: Label the pricing basis clearly wherever filters and card prices appear, e.g. 'per night' vs '3-night total', and keep filter ranges consistent with displayed card prices.
findings.source_hint: tokyo.html filter sidebar and hotel price cards

findings.user_goal: Finish checkout with confidence after entering required guest details
findings.problem: The reservation form gives very weak progress feedback: the primary CTA was disabled without clear explanation, and filling required fields produced little or no visible confirmation until it suddenly became enabled later.
findings.evidence: On reservation.html, 'Complete booking' was initially disabled and click attempts failed with the native disabled state. Recent mobile steps show phone, email, last name, arrival-time selection, and first name changes produced 'no obvious visible-text or URL change' and no inline guidance, yet the same CTA later became enabled and successfully navigated to confirmation.html.
findings.why_it_matters: Users in checkout need clear reassurance about what is complete and what is still blocking submission; otherwise they may re-enter data, miss a requirement, or abandon.
findings.suggestion: Show explicit inline validation and a persistent completion checklist near the CTA, including which required fields are satisfied and which still need attention.
findings.source_hint: reservation.html form fields and Complete booking button

findings.user_goal: Interpret and operate search and checkout controls with assistive technology or reduced visual context
findings.problem: Several important inputs are unlabeled or weakly labeled, especially on search and booking forms.
findings.evidence: The Tokyo and Shinjuku results destination inputs were flagged as missing labels/aria-labels/placeholders. On reservation.html, the Country/region select had a missing-label warning. On airport-taxis.html, the date/time and passenger inputs were also flagged as having no label, aria-label, or placeholder.
findings.why_it_matters: Unlabeled controls reduce comprehension for screen-reader users and also hurt sighted users when context is lost during scrolling or when prefilled values are ambiguous.
findings.suggestion: Add persistent visible labels and matching programmatic labels to all core inputs, especially destination, country/region, passenger count, and pickup time fields.
findings.source_hint: tokyo.html, shinjuku.html, reservation.html, airport-taxis.html form controls

findings.user_goal: Tap key controls accurately on mobile while browsing and checking out
findings.problem: Many mobile controls are too small for comfortable touch interaction, including some important navigation and form choices.
findings.evidence: Observations repeatedly flagged sub-44px targets such as header nav items, Booking.com brand link, JPY control, breadcrumb links, review links, 'Change your selection', and 13x13px radio/checkbox targets on reservation.html for guest selection and special requests.
findings.why_it_matters: Small targets increase mistaps, slow down completion, and particularly hurt users trying to complete checkout one-handed or with limited dexterity.
findings.suggestion: Increase touch target size and spacing for mobile, prioritizing form radios/checkboxes, header actions, breadcrumbs, and secondary controls within the booking funnel.
findings.source_hint: reservation.html mobile controls; hotel-detail-granbell.html and room-selection.html mobile nav/secondary controls

findings.user_goal: Compare search results and use nearby controls without accidental navigation
findings.problem: Hotel cards appear to have oversized clickable areas, making it easy to navigate into a detail page when trying to interact with nearby controls like sorting.
findings.evidence: During sort testing on tokyo.html, attempts intended for sort-related controls instead activated the Park Hyatt result card and navigated to hotel-detail.html. Reflections note this suggests a broad clickable hotel card area and accidental navigation risk, with recovery only available via '← Back to results'.
findings.why_it_matters: Unexpected page changes interrupt comparison shopping, especially when users are trying to refine or sort rather than commit to one property.
findings.suggestion: Tighten card hit areas so only explicit card CTAs/titles navigate, and visually separate sorting/filtering controls from clickable result cards.
findings.source_hint: tokyo.html hotel cards near sort controls

findings.user_goal: Assess whether a hotel matches expectations before booking
findings.problem: The Shinjuku Granbell hotel detail page uses placeholder-style hero imagery instead of believable photos.
findings.evidence: Chunk observations for hotel-detail-granbell.html state the hero gallery shows large colored placeholder tiles with emoji/icons rather than real hotel photography.
findings.why_it_matters: For accommodation decisions, photos are a primary trust and decision input; placeholder imagery makes the listing feel unfinished and less credible.
findings.suggestion: Replace placeholder gallery tiles with real property images or, if unavailable, clearly label the gallery as sample/coming soon rather than presenting it as the main photo area.

findings.user_goal: Get help or use support/discovery links after booking or while exploring
findings.problem: Several support and footer links appear to be dead ends, which weakens recovery and site credibility.
findings.evidence: Across deals, help-adjacent, airport-taxis, attractions, and final confirmation observations, items like 'Manage your trips', 'Contact Customer Service', 'Genius loyalty program', 'Privacy & cookies', 'Terms & conditions', 'Extranet login', and 'List your property' were noted as linking to '#'.
findings.why_it_matters: Users often rely on these links when uncertain or after booking; dead-end support links reduce trust and make the experience feel incomplete.
findings.suggestion: Prioritize wiring support, legal, and account-management footer links to real destinations, especially on confirmation and promotional pages where reassurance matters most.
findings.source_hint: confirmation.html footer; deals.html / airport-taxis.html / attractions.html footer links

gaps: Only directly exercised 9% of visible interactive feature signatures.
15 browser action(s) failed and should be retried or analyzed.
